post_title: How many drones will Russia launch at Ukraine overnight on 26–27 November 2026?

question.title: How many drones will Russia launch at Ukraine overnight on 26–27 November 2026?
question.description:
Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine is in its fifth winter, and Moscow has renewed a large-scale air campaign against Ukraine's power grid. President Volodymyr Zelensky said on 13 November 2026 that Russia has struck Ukrainian energy facilities more than 310 times since 1 November; Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi reported damage to major high-voltage substations in six oblasts overnight on 10–11 November and in nine oblasts on the night of 12–13 November, with power cuts affecting up to 12 oblasts. More than 600,000 consumers in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast were without power over the weekend of 7–8 November, and grid operator Ukrenergo has kept all-day blackout schedules in place in parts of the country, warning that repeat strikes wreck equipment before repairs can be completed. The UN Security Council discussed the strikes on 9 November 2026, with UN officials warning that they threaten millions of civilians ahead of winter.

Diplomacy is running in parallel. Trilateral Ukraine–Russia–US talks were held in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November 2026, the first such round since February; they produced agreement on a large prisoner exchange but no consensus on ceasefire arrangements, an energy truce, or territorial issues. Kyiv had sought a maritime and energy ceasefire at technical level, while Moscow rejected an immediate ceasefire. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow on 12 November and Zelensky in Dublin on 13 November; a further round was agreed, with European representatives joining, but as of 13 November no date had been set — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only that it would take place "in the foreseeable future". A limited energy ceasefire attempted in March 2025 collapsed, and Putin publicly ruled out a ceasefire in a speech on 1 October 2026.

The practical observable of this campaign is the size of the overnight drone barrages reported each morning by the Ukrainian Air Force. Recent nightly totals of drones launched (all types): 193 (night of 1–2 Nov), 289 (2–3 Nov), 310 (3–4 Nov), 164 (7–8 Nov), 317 (8–9 Nov), 162 (9–10 Nov), 163 (10–11 Nov) and 117 (12–13 Nov). Ukraine's General Staff reported 3,519 attack drones launched in the first ten days of November. Russian output has risen through 2026: the Institute for Science and International Security puts the 2026 average launch rate at roughly 200–220 UAVs per day, with three nights above 600 total UAVs in April 2026, while the largest single-night barrage of the war remains 7 September 2025 (810 Shahed-type drones). Jet-powered Shaheds now make up a large share of each barrage, and analysts expect heavy strikes to continue through the winter, punctuated by lulls or surges around diplomatic developments.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the number of drones that the Ukrainian Air Force reports as launched by Russian forces at Ukraine in its overnight summary for the night of 26–27 November 2026 — the summary first published on the morning of 27 November 2026 (Kyiv time), covering whatever overnight period that summary itself states. The resolving figure is the aggregate "launched" total given in that summary and published in English by [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/) or [Ukrinform's war feed](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato) — i.e., the number in reports headlined along the lines of "Russia launches N drones at Ukraine overnight". Example of scale: a report stating that Russia attacked with 310 drones, of which 272 were downed, resolves as 310 (entered as 310). If the summary reports that no drones were launched at Ukraine in that window, the question resolves as 0. If the Air Force's figure for this attack window is not published by either outlet, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the Air Force's figures will be used.
question.fine_print: Drones of all types count: Shahed/Geran strike drones (including jet-powered variants) and decoy drones such as Gerbera and Parodiya. Missiles of any kind (cruise, ballistic or aeroballistic) are not counted. If the Air Force summary gives per-type drone counts but no aggregate total, the value is the sum of the reported drone counts. If the Air Force publishes both an overnight figure for the night of 26–27 November and a separate combined 24-hour figure, the overnight figure is used. If more than one figure for this overnight window is published, the latest figure published before 12:00 UTC on 27 November 2026 is used.
